additions.what: Emphasized that treatment assignment creates a covariate shift in the problem context
additions.why: Students consistently miss that propensity weights ARE covariate shift weights, not a separate type of adjustment

additions.what: Added desirable property about recognizing counterfactual inference as fundamentally a covariate shift problem
additions.why: This is the paper's key conceptual insight that students keep missing by proposing more complex frameworks

removals.what: Removed mention of 'study population differs from target population' and related complexity
removals.why: This was leading students to propose doubly-weighted approaches when the paper shows a single weighting suffices

removals.what: Removed several desirable properties about robustness and handling different subject types
removals.why: Too many properties were distracting from the core insight about covariate shift

removals.what: Simplified field context to focus on the unexplored connection between weighted conformal and propensity weighting
removals.why: Previous version was too broad and not pointing clearly enough to the specific connection

rationale.unchanged: Kept the emphasis on finite-sample guarantees and model-free approaches as these are correctly identified by students as key aspects
